chapter: Small band, Charlie Parker and the big band
title: Losing the value of money on the big band
summary: He admits he was worse with money once he had a big band and refused to downsize after the Army.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Well, now, when you were talking about your father and big business like, now, when you get this big band, you sort of, being a good businessman --

No, I was worse, I got worse, because I was like this. If a guy says, 'Well, man, I see a horn I want.' If I had the money, I'd say, 'Well, can you do better? Can you do this? Get it.' I lost -- I liked the big band so well that I lost the value of money. I lost the value of money so that when I come out of the service, they told me, they says, 'Now you out of the service, but things have changed. Now, get you a small group and we'll get the same money for a small group you'll get for a big band.' 'No,' I says, 'I want the big
Well, I mean, you know, that -- you can look back now and see what -- but at that time, everybody was still thinking in terms of big bands, weren't they?
